Mr. Market is pricing in a highly skeptical outlook for Dow Inc. at $30.48, viewing the recent Q2 2026 operational spike as an unsustainable cyclical peak. The market is heavily discounting the $12.1 billion quarterly revenue run-rate, focusing instead on the immediate $0.15-per-pound drop in North American polyethylene prices in June 2026 and management's subsequent guidance of a 26% sequential collapse in Q3 2026 EBITDA to $1.7 billion. This pricing reflects a belief in structural terminal decay rather than a normal cyclical trough. The market is fixated on the persistent volume erosion—evidenced by a 1% year-over-year decline in global volumes despite a 20% surge in net sales—and the ongoing financial drain of the Sadara joint venture, which carries a $1.3 billion debt guarantee. By valuing the company at 26.3x EV/OE, the market is signaling that Dow's high-cost European assets are structurally uncompetitive and that its flagship "Path to Zero" decarbonization project delay to 2029 will permanently impair its long-term capital efficiency and dividend sustainability.

How Things Are Going Now

Dow Inc. is navigating a classic cyclical trough characterized by volatile regional spreads and aggressive operational self-help execution. Across the trailing four quarters, revenue has demonstrated choppy sequential behavior, moving from a trough run-rate near $38B annualized up to a recent quarterly surge in mid-2026 that pushed annualized run-rate revenue to $48,368.0M with gross margins hovering around 9.8%. Management has captured localized pricing gains and expanded in-year self-help benefits under the Transform to Outperform program to greater than $1.3 billion, helping stabilize operating EBITDA during periods of macro softness.

Underneath the headline figures, active merchant volumes in Packaging and Specialty Plastics experienced localized headwinds, including minor volume contractions driven by planned maintenance activity and plant turnarounds. However, temporary polyethylene price spikes in North America drove quarterly operating EBITDA higher before management guided an anticipated sequential moderation due to subsequent contract price normalization. Cash generation has recovered moderately, with operating cash flow and free cash flow turning positive as working capital builds are managed against revenue growth.

Capital allocation remains strictly defensive. Management has prioritized debt reduction over shareholder returns, halting share buybacks entirely while maintaining the quarterly common dividend at $0.35 per share following its reduction in late 2025. Simultaneously, capital expenditures are being tightly controlled, with outlays actively scrutinized or evaluated for joint-venture equity partners to preserve balance sheet liquidity.
